elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.1 as rendered: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... shall not exceed the greater of ..." and "The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims." Pre-existing mutual language retained verbatim.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: 21.1 now reads "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000." Basis is "fees paid or payable" (not broader "all amounts"), lookback runs to the claim, and the USD 1,000,000 floor is present. The lowercase "fees ... under this Agreement and all Order Forms" deliberately escapes the illusory defined term "Fees" (1.5/1.6 = one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee) and drops the "first Order Form" limiter.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.2 retained unchanged: "neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill"; the favourable direct-damages sentence (restoration of Customer Data, replacement services, notices, incident response) is preserved.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims (carved out of both 21.1 and 21.2) include "a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations"; retained verbatim.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Same Excluded Claims definition expressly lists "data-protection, or security obligations"; 21.1/21.2 both open "Except for Excluded Claims".
21.3: "its indemnification obligations" is an Excluded Claim, so indemnities sit outside the cap (no super-cap issue).
21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" listed as Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" is an Excluded Claim; mutual in direction ("a Party's ... the other Party's").

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: 21.3 final sentence now reads "Customer's obligations to pay amounts due under this Agreement and any Order Form are not damages and are not limited by this Section." This covers Customer's payment obligations as a whole rather than the narrow defined "Fees" (Implementation Fee only) qualified by "undisputed ... for conforming Services". The deterministic check returned false, but that is a literal-string mismatch (no phrase "payment obligations"); in substance the carve-out is complete and untethered to the illusory Fees definition.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the two operations fix the only two defective elements (cap basis and payment carve-out), and every remaining preferred element was already present in 21.1–21.3 and is retained verbatim.

The original cap was walk-away (aggregate liability effectively USD 12,000 because "Fees" = the one-time Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, well below six months' fees); the reset to lowercase "fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms" with a USD 1,000,000 floor cures that. Classification as a deviation is correct.

Minimality holds: edits are confined to the cap formula in 21.1 and the payment sentence in 21.3. Deleting "undisputed" and "for conforming Services" was necessary, not cosmetic — retaining them would have left the carve-out as a narrow subset rather than Customer payment obligations as a whole. No survival tails, procedures, examples or extra damages categories were added, and the Customer-favourable direct-damages language in 21.2 and the whole Excluded Claims list are untouched.

Intent is preserved: no dangling cross-references; 21.3 no longer relies on the "Fees" definition, and 1.5/1.6 remain intact for the payment/ordering mechanics that use them. Residual drafting risk to monitor (not a failure): 21.1 relies on lowercase "fees" coexisting with the capitalised defined term "Fees"; if the counterparty pushes back, consider amending 1.5 to define Fees as all amounts payable under all Order Forms rather than leaving the case distinction to do the work.

Fallback is also satisfied a fortiori (mutual cap, 12-month fee basis, indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct all uncapped), so the redline is position-complete at both levels.
